payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Add order priority and backorders end-to-end
root.objective: Ship priority-aware ordering, backorder recording, analytics, API exposure, SVG rendering, and a deterministic g6 probe without breaking existing behavior
expectedOutcomes: Priority defaults to standard and invalid supplied values fail fast in the domain layer.
Shortages produce recorded backorders instead of hard reservation failures where the domain now allows cancellation.
Downstream layers compile against the shared order/backorder contract and consume the recorded backorder event where needed.
Express orders are prioritized within a wave, analytics count backorders, the API returns current backorders, and the SVG distinguishes order priority.
The new g6 probe behaves like the existing probes and emits deterministic JSON-only stdout.

complexitySignals.rationale: The change crosses shared domain contracts and several downstream layers, so the root must stay broad enough to preserve compile-time and behavioral coupling.

cut.rationale: The work is best split by stable layer boundaries because the domain contract, service event flow, fulfillment ordering, analytics, API response, SVG rendering, and probe behavior can each be verified independently while sharing the same underlying order/backorder semantics.

children.title: Extend the orders domain contract
children.objective: Add order priority defaults and validation, backorder recording, cancellable shortage handling, and listBackorders(state) in the domain model
expectedOutcomes: Orders accept an optional priority at the call site and treat omission as standard.
Supplying any unsupported priority throws OrderError.
Shortages create recorded Backorder entries instead of throwing immediately.
WarehouseState carries backorders keyed by order id and listBackorders(state) returns them all.

children.title: Wire the warehouse service to backorders
children.objective: Expose the new service operations and emit a warehouse event whenever a backorder is recorded
expectedOutcomes: The service forwards the new priority-aware order flow into the domain without breaking existing callers.
Backorder recording is surfaced as a warehouse event that downstream consumers can process.
Existing service behavior remains intact for non-backordered orders.

children.title: Prioritize express orders within a wave
children.objective: Keep the existing planner signature and reorder each wave so express orders are listed before standard ones
expectedOutcomes: Within a single wave, express orders are planned ahead of standard orders.
The planner signature stays unchanged.
Wave grouping and other existing planner behavior continue to work.

children.title: Count backorders in journal analytics
children.objective: Derive a backorders count from persisted events in HistoryAnalytics
expectedOutcomes: Journal analytics includes a backorders count derived from the event history.
The count stays consistent with recorded backorder events.
Existing journal analytics remain unchanged apart from the new field.

children.title: Expose backorders through the API server
children.objective: Return the current state's backorders from the server without regressing existing responses
expectedOutcomes: The server response includes the current state backorders.
Existing API behavior stays stable for the rest of the payload.
The backorder data reflects the same domain state that the service and journal use.

children.title: Render priority differences in the tower SVG
children.objective: Make the SVG distinguish express orders from standard orders using the existing presentation pipeline
expectedOutcomes: Express orders render with a distinct visual treatment from standard orders.
The SVG stays compatible with existing layout and rendering behavior.
The distinction is observable in the rendered output and covered by tests.

children.title: Add the g6 study probe and script
children.objective: Add src/probe/g6.ts plus a study:g6-probe package script that emits one deterministic JSON object and nothing else when run directly
expectedOutcomes: main() returns a JSON string.
Direct execution writes exactly one JSON object to stdout with no other output.
Two runs from the same commit produce byte-identical output.
The new script is available in package.json and follows the shape of the existing probes.

Journal analytics are derived here, so backorders count belongs in this module.
Existing journal tests can cover the new analytics field without changing test placement.
The server is the API surface that must expose current-state backorders.
Existing API tests are the correct regression point for response shape changes.
The tower renderer owns the SVG that must visually distinguish express from standard orders.

The probe CLI shows the existing probe shape that the new g6 probe should follow.

An existing probe script establishes the repository's current probe execution pattern.
The test script already scans src/probe/*.test.ts, which supports placing the new g6 probe test beside the code it covers.
The repository is TypeScript-based, so the new cross-layer contract changes need to stay type-safe across exported interfaces and tests.
